        - text: DISCRETE AND APPLIED MATHEMATICS FINANCIAL MATHEMATICS AND MODELLING

        - paragraph: Compare scenarios under the same time and starting assumptions.
      - complementary: "Lesson: 605 Level: Intermediate-Advanced Time: 6-10 min Lab: Applied Modelling Lab"
      - navigation:
        - button "Interact"
        - button "Learn"
        - button "Worked Example"
        - button "Formula"

      - text: LEARNING SEQUENCE
      - article: 1 Observe See how two plans grow.
      - article: 2 Manipulate Adjust the controls.
      - article: 3 Notice the pattern Compare curves and values.
      - article: 4 Understand the rule Grasp the math behind it.
      - article: 5 Try independently Apply in a challenge.
      - complementary:
        - heading "CONTROL PANEL" [level=3]
        - text: Starting capital (Rs)
        - spinbutton "Starting capital (Rs)": "20000"
        - slider "Starting capital (Rs) slider": "20000"
        - text: 1,000 to 100,000 Plan A rate (p.a.)
        - spinbutton "Plan A rate (p.a.)": "6"
        - slider "Plan A rate (p.a.) slider": "6"
        - text: 0 to 25% Plan B rate (p.a.)
        - spinbutton "Plan B rate (p.a.)": "8"
        - slider "Plan B rate (p.a.) slider": "8"
        - text: 0 to 25% Time horizon (years)
        - spinbutton "Time horizon (years)": "5"
        - slider "Time horizon (years) slider": "5"
        - text: 1 to 30 Fees (% of balance p.a.)
        - spinbutton "Fees (% of balance p.a.)": "1"
        - slider "Fees (% of balance p.a.) slider": "1"
        - text: 0 to 5% Risk/volatility
        - combobox "Risk volatility":
          - option "Low"
          - option "Moderate" [selected]
          - option "High"
        - button "Reset to defaults":
          - img
          - text: Reset to defaults
      - main:
        - text: INVESTMENT COMPARISON MODEL Plan A (6% p.a.) | Plan B (8% p.a.)
        - img "Investment growth comparison graph": 50,000 40,000 30,000 20,000 10,000 0 0 20,000 1 2 3 4 5 27,946.33
        - text: "Break-even (crossover): Plan B leads from year 0"
        - article:
          - text: Plan A Summary
          - strong: Rs 25,452.78
          - paragraph: Final value after year 5
          - text: "Effective return (p.a.): 4.94%"
        - article:
          - text: Plan B Summary
          - strong: Rs 27,946.33
          - paragraph: Final value after year 5
          - text: "Effective return (p.a.): 6.92%"
        - complementary:
          - text: Key readout
          - paragraph:
            - text: Plan B yields
            - strong: Rs 2,493.54
            - text: more at year 5.
      - article:
        - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Both plans start with Rs 20,000.00. Fees are 1% p.a.
        - paragraph: Plan A effective factor = 1.0494
        - paragraph: Plan B effective factor = 1.0692
        - paragraph:
          - text: FV
          - subscript: A
          - text: = Rs 25,452.78
        - paragraph:
          - text: FV
          - subscript: B
          - text: = Rs 27,946.33
      - article:
        - heading "KEY RULE / DEFINITION" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Future value with fees
        - strong:
          - text: FV = P[(1 + r)(1 - f)]
          - superscript: "n"
        - paragraph: P = starting capital r = nominal annual rate f = annual fee rate n = number of years
      - article:
        - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Adding rates instead of compounding.
        - paragraph: "Incorrect: P(1 + nr)"
        - paragraph: "Why it is wrong: It ignores growth on growth."
        - paragraph:
          - text: "Always use: P(1 + r)"
          - superscript: "n"
          - text: ", adjusted for fees."
      - heading "QUICK CHALLENGE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: With the same starting capital, fees of 1% p.a. and 5 years, what nominal annual rate must Plan A earn to match Plan B's final value of Rs 27,946.33?
      - text: Your answer
      - textbox "Matching annual rate"
      - text: "%"
      - button "Check Answer"

        - button "Show solution"
